artikel.titel: Rates Spark: Bank of England likely to join the hiking club
artikel.text: A win for the Democrats helped Brent oil ease below $100, benefiting European government bonds. But we cannot ignore a 4% eurozone inflation reading, showing higher energy costs are already passing through the economy. The same story applies to the UK, where the Bank of England will likely hike rates. But with 24bp already priced in, this won't be a surprise

artikel.titel: FX Daily: A dollar downturn lacks the rate ingredient
artikel.text: The post-midterm dollar correction requires a worsening of USD rate differentials to turn into a downturn. But as oil prices fall, other central banks are facing similar or even larger dovish repricing than the Fed. Data is key now, but indications are that they won’t turn USD-negative soon. Today, expect a hike in the UK and rate holds in Norway and Mexico

artikel.titel: Philippine inflation spikes, but BSP likely to hike only 25bp in December
artikel.text: ASIA/PACIFIC: The Philippines’ inflation surge to 7.8% in October was substantial, driven largely by energy price shocks. However, if oil prices continue to ease, third-quarter growth proves soft, and the peso extends its recent gains, we expect the central bank to scale back to a 25bp hike in December

artikel.titel: The Commodities Feed: Oil plunges following US midterm elections
artikel.text: Energy markets are under significant pressure following the Democrats’ clean sweep in the US midterms as hopes grow that the political shift could accelerate efforts to bring the war with Iran to an end

artikel.titel: National Bank of Poland holds rates despite higher 2027 inflation forecast
artikel.text: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: The National Bank of Poland (NBP) kept rates unchanged in November despite a sharp upgrade to its 2027 inflation forecast. With the price shock still manifesting in energy and limited signs of second-round effects, we think the NBP can afford to wait, with any rate hikes unlikely before early 2027

artikel.titel: Tech now accounts for two-thirds of the US trade deficit
artikel.text: NORTH AMERICA: There has been a lot of commentary about the contribution of tech investment to GDP growth, but with the US running a trade deficit of $64bn in September in tech products alone, out of an overall trade deficit of $105bn, we need to remember that this aspect actually subtracts from growth. Instead, it is a boon to the likes of Korea and Taiwan

artikel.titel: France’s social demands run up against tightening fiscal constraints
artikel.text: EUROPE: Thursday’s nationwide mobilisation over wages and purchasing power will add pressure on a French government already struggling with weak growth, a fragile labour market and an increasingly unmanageable budget. Its options for responding to social discontent are narrowing as higher borrowing costs further weaken the outlook for public debt

artikel.titel: Uzbekistan rates stay on hold, but hopes for 2027 cuts remain
artikel.text: COMMONWEALTH OF INDEPENDENT STATES: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan kept its policy rate unchanged at 14.00%, as expected, but delivered a more hawkish message than in September. Higher inflation and GDP forecasts suggest that easing in 2026 is now less likely. But we still see scope for cuts in 2027, assuming continued fiscal restraint and potential FX strength

artikel.titel: Rates Outlook 2027: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
artikel.text: The spaghetti-western title neatly captures the three big forces shaping long-end rates: the ‘good’ of AI-driven productivity, the ‘bad’ of elevated fiscal deficits, and the ‘ugly’ of renewed inflationary pressure from ongoing wars. By the middle of 2027, however, things should start to look a little less ugly as inflation falls
